newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer CEO predicts record profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Bayer CEO predicts record profit in 1997.

text.p: German chemicals giant Bayer AG will announce a record net profit of 2.6 billion marks for 1996, raising the prospect of a higher dividend, chief executive Manfred Schneider told the Spiegel news weekly.
Spiegel, in an article released on Saturday, quoted Schneider as saying he saw a good chance that Bayer's supervisory board would share his support for a dividend increase.
"We have always said that we would link our payouts to earnings," Schneider said in extracts from the interview.
Bayer made a group net profit of 2.4 billion marks in 1995, on which it paid a 15 mark dividend.
Despite expected profit gains, Schneider said Bayer would not create any new jobs in Germany because of high taxes, high labour overheads and over-regulation.
"These disadvantages have compelled us and will continue to force us to reduce jobs. We will not, for the foreseeable future, create any new jobs in Germany," he told Spiegel.
